comments.author: @GeisterNachti
comments.text: The video answers the question correctly from an accounting perspective but underestimates the economic significance of public debt. While bank lending creates money but no net financial assets within the private sector, government deficits increase the net financial assets of the non-government sector. Well-directed public spending can increase employment, productivity, and prosperity. From an MMT perspective, the fundamental constraint on a monetarily sovereign government is not its debt-to-GDP ratio, but the availability of real resources, productive capacity, and the risk of inflation. What ultimately matters is not debt itself, but its economic impact.

comments.author: @sakibpratyay
comments.text:
Look at the map when everyone's debt is painted red—$365 trillion across the world, roughly three times everything humanity produces in a year—and ask the question nobody in a tailored suit wants to answer out loud: if everybody owes money, who is collecting? 

Follow the chain past the polite accounting excuses and you find a machine built to trap the people at the bottom while shielding the people at the top. 

Banks type numbers into accounts when they make loans and wipe them out when loans get paid; governments issue bonds to their own trust funds and central banks; pension funds and savings accounts sit wired into the middle of the whole thing. When the bill breaks—in Cyprus, in Greece, in Lebanon—it isn't the untouchable architects who get gutted first; it's savers, pensioners, and ordinary people watching their money get locked, haircutted, or eaten alive by inflation.

Meanwhile, look where the real leverage and the sharpest blind spots sit. Trillions in claims move through custody hubs and offshore jurisdictions—the Cayman Islands, Luxembourg, London, clearinghouses where official tables miss massive chunks of hedge-fund Treasury positions, and an ~$8.4 trillion gap between what countries report being owed and what debtor nations report owing. 

At home, the top slice of households holds the lion's share of direct government bonds and collects the interest flowing out of national budgets day after day, while younger generations and working households carry the mortgages, the bills, and the shrinking room to breathe. This is literally eating away at humanity's lifeforce, mortgaging the children and their children's children for consumption done by current decision makers. They/we have been selling our future generations into slavery willingly.

Wrap that in the legal and monetary machinery built across the City of London, its offshore orbit, and the shift from Bretton Woods to fiat debt, and look what happens to every elected government and every newborn child. Private wealth and multi-family offices can move across borders, jurisdictions, and trusts like water through pipes; The asset management firms also owns the banks' voting, not just the two party carnival to keep people occupied and fighting amongst themselves for admission into the fun slaughterhouse. An elected government has to stand there on a shrinking plank and service the debt, keep the lights on, and answer to voters who have no exit door. And every baby born into that order doesn't arrive free with a blank slate—they walk out of the delivery room with an iron ball already chained to their ankle, paying for a ledger they never signed while the people who built the chain keep their money safely out of reach.
